modelType.description: Registry model type: chat is a Pi chat model, classifier is a Pi built-in classifier via modelRegistry.classify.

classifier.description: Classifier verdict thresholds — pure policy, no transport knobs.

confidenceThreshold.description: Minimum confidence at which a classifier reading is adopted (0–1, default 0.5); below it that axis takes its uncertainty path. Compares the returned confidence (the label distribution's peak concentration); it does not measure evidence completeness.

fallbacks.description: Ordered backup reviewers (defaults to none). Entries use Pi registry provider/model ids; a classifier entry runs through modelRegistry.classify.

temperature.description: Overrides the top-level temperature for this entry, which wins because a backup is a different model.

maxTokens.description: Reviewer answer budget in tokens. With reasoning on, budget-based providers (Anthropic, Bedrock) add the thinking budget on top, while effort-based providers (OpenAI-compatible) share this cap with thinking; too small a cap truncates the reply mid-think (the empty-reply machinery failure).

temperature.description: Sampling temperature for both lanes. Unset leaves the field off the wire, so the provider default applies. 0 makes two reviews of one request agree; leave it unset for a model that rejects non-default sampling, such as an OpenAI reasoning model. Backends without a sampling knob ignore it (TypeSafe carries none).

mode.description: The leniency ladder for the reviewer's non-allow verdicts, strictest first. Only the deterministic screen hard-denies: a model deny is soft whatever riskLevel it reports, and riskLevel is an audit label that never picks the tier. The model's own uncertainty is split by its lean (benign-leaned, neutral, danger-leaned): 'strict' — everything denies, the reviewer's allow is the only pass; 'default' — you judge every flag but hard danger, so soft denies and every unresolved doubt ask; 'auto' — no prompt is ever raised, benign and neutral doubts pass, danger-leaned doubts and every deny deny. 'auto' is not the yolo mode of Codex, Claude Code, or Gemini CLI: those neither ask nor block, while auto still blocks every deny and every danger-leaned doubt. Reviewer machinery failures never map to allow: they deny under strict and auto, and defer under default. 'custom' runs the two cut lines and the failure lane from customMode; it is only selectable while that block is present, and an unconfigured custom falls back to 'default' with a config issue.

customMode.description: The operator-defined ladder row, read only when mode is 'custom'. Two cut lines, the reviewer-failure lane, and the irreversible axis, nothing else: a mode is two boundaries plus two lanes, so a custom row is contiguous by construction and cannot express an incoherent per-rung table. allowThrough at or above denyFrom is legal and leaves no ask band (the mode never prompts); the footer then renders it in warning red once the casual cycle can reach it. A pair drawing exactly a built-in row with the defer ruling is reported as redundant.

allowThrough.description: At or below this rung the mode allows (inclusive). 'defer-neutral' is the ask-free-but-still-blocking posture: benign and neutral doubts pass, danger-leaned doubts deny.

denyFrom.description: At or above this rung the mode denies (inclusive). The deterministic screen's hard deny is terminal in every mode.

onReviewFailure.description: How a review that produced no verdict is disposed of. Never allow: a broken reviewer must not rubber-stamp.

onIrreversibleEffect.description: How a reviewer allow that met a proven-irreversible effect is disposed of. Its own axis, not a rung on the suspicion line: 'defer' asks (what every built-in rung does), 'allow' passes the class the operator accepts, 'deny' blocks it. The deterministic screen's hard deny stays terminal regardless.

notifyLevel.description: The minimum ambient (review-loop) notification level that still notifies the operator; 'off' silences all ambient notices. Command feedback (the /ai-guard surface) is never gated. With denials having no host dialog, 'off' or 'warning' means model denies (and clarifications, at 'warning') reach only the agent and the audit log.

notifyApprovals.description: Opt in to info-level notices when AI Guard emits an allow (fresh or cached). Fresh reviews carry their total review cost in a duration tail; cache replays say (cached). Mapped allows name the mode (`mode (auto) allowed without asking`); path and external_directory families are excluded because the host caps their allows to defer. Subject to notifyLevel; commands and targets are never shown.

anyOf.description: Broadcast custom safety rules: the same content is appended to every lane (chat `rules`, classifier `background`).

chat.description: Chat-lane slot: custom safety rules. `replace: true` swaps the built-in rules for them instead of appending; the verdict contract is always appended either way.

background.description: Shared background text or structured context appended to every question.

questions.description: Per-question additions keyed by question id.

classifier.description: Classifier-lane slot (append-only): shared background plus per-question additions keyed by stable axis question id. The built-in reviewer background, questions, and criteria are the answer contract the verdict thresholds are calibrated against, so nothing here replaces them.

anyOf.description: Per-lane slots. A lane without a slot runs the built-in instructions; a slot whose lane no configured reviewer declares is rejected. A lane declared only by a fallback can still go unused if that fallback is later skipped — the loader reports it.
